column1: # B.6 for algorithms: the domains `method` axis against the algorithms dimension.
# Written 2026-10-07. STRUCTURE against STRUCTURE -- never sample against sample,
# because the algorithms vocabulary available today was drawn through the models[]
# slot and is biased ~5x toward RL, so a sample-level comparison would measure two
# differently-biased samples rather than the two ontologies.
# verdict: axis    -- the branch asks the same question as a whole algorithms axis
#          lineage -- its children name algorithms lineage families
#          split   -- the branch straddles models and algorithms
#          none    -- genuinely disjoint, and should stay so

column4: the algorithms `signal` axis (S.src.*), plus A.regime and A.agents
column5: This branch and that axis answer the same question. supervised/self-supervised/RL are S.src.ext.human / S.src.self.* / S.src.env.reward; online-vs-offline RL is A.regime; multi-agent is A.agents.

column4: L.da, L.mtl, L.cont, L.meta, L.fed, L.dpar, L.sched
column5: Every child names an algorithms lineage family almost one-to-one.

column4: L.sgd/L.derivfree, L.mcmc, L.vi, L.seq.pf, L.causal, L.graphalg, L.tts, L.dec, L.marl.game
column5: The largest overlapping branch. Probabilistic inference, causal inference, search, planning and inference procedures are all algorithms families.

column4: neural-architectures -> MODELS; generative-models -> mixed; model-efficiency -> L.prune, L.quant, L.kd, L.lowrankc
column5: The branch straddles three dimensions, which is what B.6 predicted for models and found there as zero lexical overlap.
Interpretability, adversarial ML and uncertainty quantification are all algorithms families.

GENUINELY DISJOINT. Generalization, sample complexity, expressivity, training dynamics and scaling behaviour are properties studied, not procedures executed. Nothing in the algorithms dimension corresponds, and nothing should.
Data synthesis, selection and annotation are algorithms families under the widened scope.
A disposal branch for generic strings; no counterpart by design.
